New Temporary & Permanent Course Email
Date: October 30, 2026 (2026-10-30)
Tags: Temp Course Email
New Temporary & Permanent Course Email
The New Temporary & Permanent Course Email is distributed to all faculty, deans, and associate and assistant deans on the last weekday of each month. Recipients then have seven days to submit comments to the CASC Chair, GEC Chair, or Dean of the Graduate School regarding any potential or perceived content overlap involving a new temporary or permanent course.
The email serves two purposes:
Provides notice of upcoming Faculty Senate review. Courses included in the email have already been reviewed and approved by their respective College Curriculum Committees and will next be reviewed by the appropriate Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee: CASC, GEC, or Graduate Council.
Provides an opportunity to identify potential content overlap. College Curriculum Committees may review the courses included in the email to identify any potential or perceived overlap with courses offered or proposed by other colleges. Any concerns can then be raised before the courses proceed to Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee review.

New Program Proposal Walkthrough
New Program Proposal Walkthrough
This guide provides step-by-step procedural instructions for completing and submitting a New Program Proposal in Kuali. It focuses on navigating the form, including what to select or enter in each field.
*In Kuali, Programs refer to Degrees, Majors, Minors & Certificates.
The guide is organized by proposal section (panel), so you can jump directly to a section when you need help.
This guide does not provide guidance on course content or academic decisions. Consult your department and applicable curriculum committees for questions about developing the course itself.
Navigate by Section
Related toolkit entry: Specialization Modification Proposal Walkthrough

Familiarize yourself with URI’s curricular process before beginning your proposal. This will help you understand the steps involved in the curricular process and accurately estimate how long your proposal may take to reach approval.
How the Curriculum Process Works
Related toolkit entry: How the Curriculum Process Works
Approval Calendar
Related toolkit entry: Approval Calendar

You will need access to Kuali Curriculum Management (Kuali CM) to propose any curricular item.
Kuali Basics
Related toolkit entry: Kuali Basics

From your browser, navigate to Kuali Curriculum Management (CM).
Select Curriculum to open your Dashboard .
Related toolkit entry: Dashboard
From the left-hand navigation menu, select Programs.
On the Programs page, select + New Program in the upper-right corner.
The following sections of this walkthrough are grouped by section of the proposal form.

Complete the following fields with your contact information.
Proposer Name Your name is automatically populated based on your Kuali account.
Proposer Title Enter your university role.
Proposer Email Enter your URI email address. This is the email reviewers will use if they have questions about your proposal.
Additional Proposer(s) Use this section to identify additional individuals who can speak to the proposed program. Individuals listed here will not receive Kuali notifications or have access to edit the proposal. Their inclusion simply provides transparency to the reviewing committees about who else is involved in or can speak to the proposal.

Effective Term & Year Select the term and year in which you intend the program to become effective. If the selected effective term has passed the applicable deadline by the time the proposal reaches the Faculty Senate, it will automatically be updated to the next available term.
First Graduation Term Select the term and year in which you anticipate the first students will graduate with this credential.
Credential Type Select the type of credential you are proposing: Degree, Major, Minor, or Certificate.
Level Select the level of the program: Undergraduate, Graduate, or Dual Currently, the only Dual Degree program offered at URI is the Pharm.D.
Academic Calendar Select the academic calendar for the program: Accelerated 7-week through URI Online, or Traditional 14-week with Summer and J-Term Sessions.
Program Locations Select all locations where the program will be offered.
College Select the college in which the program is housed.
Department Select the department in which the program is housed.
CIP Code Enter the specific CIP code that applies to your program. You can search for your program’s code here.

Is this interdisciplinary? The intent of this question is to identify whether the program is jointly owned by multiple academic departments. If yes, the percentage of ownership assigned to each department must be provided in the curriculum worksheet.
🔽 The following field will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Is this interdisciplinary?
Additional Department(s) and College(s) Enter departments sharing ownership of this program.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Degree or Major is chosen for Credential Type.
Degree e.g., Bachelor of Arts
🔽 The following field will appear only if Major is chosen for Credential Type.
Major e.g., Music
Academic Program Title Major or full degree name, followed by a dash and the degree abbreviation. e.g., Music - BA
Program Description See Program Description for formatting guidance.
Related toolkit entry: Program Description
Admission Requirements See Admission Requirements for criteria
Related toolkit entry: Admission Requirements
Total program credits Enter the total number of credits required to earn the credential.
Total core course credits Enter the total number of credits required for core courses.

Total elective course credits Enter the total number of credits required for elective courses.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Level is Undergraduate or Dual.
Total general education course credits Enter the total number of required General Education credits.
List the name(s) and title(s) of the individual(s) responsible for administering the program. Enter the name of the program director, department chair, or other individual responsible for administering the program.

Attach Curriculum Worksheet Upload a curriculum worksheet outlining the courses, credits, and other requirements that make up the proposed program’s curriculum. You may use the University’s standard curriculum worksheets, or you may clearly include all requirements in a word document or PDF.
Provide responses to the following questions:
Describe the goals of the program.
Describe how the program aligns with the University’s mission and Strategic Plan.
Describe the opportunities this program provides for graduates.
Describe the demand and regional competition for this program.
Describe the intended student population and primary sources of enrollment.
Describe the extent to which the program will attract new students or draw students from existing programs.
What is the estimated number of students in the first 4 years of the program?
What is the estimated number of annual graduates at full enrollment?
What is the minimum number of years required to complete the program?

Are any new courses being proposed or developed for this program? Select Yes or No
🔽 The following field will appear only if Yes is chosen from Are any new courses being proposed or developed for this program?
Select all new courses proposed or developed in support of this program. Type the course code into the search field, then select the appropriate course from the results.
Can’t find the course? Make sure a course proposal has been started in Kuali before attempting to add it here.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Credential Type is Degree, Major, or Certificate.
Attach Assessment Plan Complete the appropriate Assessment Plan and attach it to the proposal. → Assessment Plan for Degrees and Majors → Assessment Plan for Certificates Once the proposal is submitted to the workflow, the Office for the Advancement of Teaching & Learning will be notified and will review the Assessment Plan. They will contact you directly if any follow-up or revisions are needed.
Is the program content guided by program-specific accreditation standards or other outside guidance? Select Yes or No.

Identify the accrediting body for the proposed program. Enter the name of the accrediting body, if applicable. Enter none if the program is not subject to specialized accreditation.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Yes is selected for Is the program content guided by program-specific accreditation standards or other outside guidance?
Describe how the program will meet the requirements of the accrediting body.

Provide responses and attach any applicable documentation to the following questions:
Is this program offered in partnership with another institution or organization? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following fields will appear only if Yes is selected for the question above.
Name of institution or organization
Attach signed agreement(s) for any cooperative arrangements made with named institution/organization.
Is this program associated with any transfer agreements with independent institutions?
🔽 The following fields will appear only if Yes is selected for the question above.
Name of institution
Attach transfer agreement documentation
🔽 The following field will appear only if No is selected for Is this program associated with any transfer agreements with independent institutions?
Describe the program's transfer opportunities in the absence of formal transfer agreements, including any limitations

Provide responses and attach any applicable documentation to the following questions:
STUDENT ASSISTANCE CONSIDERATIONS
Will this program be available to students under the New England Board of Higher Education’s (NEBHE) Regional Student Program? (RSP) Select Yes or No.
Are there any available assistantships, scholarships, and/or fellowships? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following fields will appear only if Yes is selected for the question above.
List available assistantships, scholarships and/or fellowships.
Supporting Documentation
ACCESSIBILITY CONSIDERATIONS
Describe how program resources, equipment, and technology comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and applicable state disability statutes.
PERSONNEL CONSIDERATIONS
Describe the faculty and support staff needed for program success.
What minimum degree, academic/technical field, and certification requirements will instructors need?
Will this program require additional or reallocated faculty or staff resources? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following fields will appear only if Yes is selected for the question above.
How many full-time equivalent (FTE) positions are required for the program?

How many FTE positions will be in tenure-track positions?
Describe any new positions required.
Describe any reassignments of existing positions.

Provide responses and attach any applicable documentation to the following questions:
🔽 The following field will appear only if Credential Type is Degree or Certificate.
Attach Budget Form Download budget form.
Will this program require resources (faculty, staff, instructional equipment, etc.) that are not currently available? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following fields will appear only if Yes is selected for the question above.
Describe the new resources needed and provide a rationale. Indicate whether these resources are needed for program implementation, ongoing operation, or both.
Will this program require the reallocation of existing institutional resources? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Yes is selected for the question above.
Describe the institutional resources that will be reallocated and explain how they will support program implementation, ongoing operation, or both.*
Will this program require any new or renovated facilities? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Yes is selected for the question above.
Describe the new or renovated facilities needed to support this proposal, including estimated expenditures.

Will this program generate new revenue or require differential tuition and/or additional fees? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Yes is selected for the question above.
Describe the projected revenues, including the assumptions used to estimate revenue and the appropriateness and feasibility of any proposed differential tuition and/or fees.
Describe the enrollment assumptions used for the financial projections, including anticipated demand, market need, regional competition, and other factors influencing enrollment estimates.

Provide responses and attach any applicable documentation to the following questions:
Has the proposed program been discussed with academic units that may have related or overlapping curricular interests? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Yes is selected for the question above.
Supporting Documentation
Describe how the proposed program is distinct from existing curricula and address any actual or perceived areas of overlap.

🔽 This section will only appear if the Credential Type is Degree, Major, or Certificate.
Provide responses and attach any applicable documentation to the following questions:
List the main subject areas to be covered by this program.
Describe the projected growth of this program.
Summarize the anticipated course offerings for this program over the next 3–5 years.
List the journals, monographs, and electronic resources the University Library must have to support this program.
List additional library resources that would enhance this program but are not essential, including journals, monographs, and electronic resources.
Describe the types of assignments in which students will conduct library research, such as locating journal articles, creating annotated bibliographies, or writing research papers. Attach additional documentation if needed.
Assignment Documents
Library Impact Statement Document Proposer: Leave this field blank. Upon submission to the workflow, the proposal will be automatically routed to the Library Subject Selector, who will complete and attach the LIS to the proposal.

Once you have finalized your proposal draft:
Select Leave Edit Mode in the upper-right corner of the screen, just below the orange bar.
Select Submit for Approval to submit the proposal to the workflow.

Your proposal will automatically be sent to the appropriate review committees. You may be contacted within Kuali Comments by the committees with questions to the proposal (an email will notify you automatically). You can also return to your proposal from your dashboard at any time to view the workflow status.
